questions.stem: TCA is an amphibolic pathway with many of its intermediates are part of other catabolic and anabolic reactions. All of the following are intermediates of the TCA cycle, except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Malonate
  • Malonate is not an intermediate of the TCA cycle
  • It is an inhibitor of:
  • TCA cycle (a competitive inhibitor of enzyme succinate dehydrogenase)
  • ETC (component inhibited is Complex II)
  • Beta Oxidation of Fatty Acids (Enz inhibited is Carnitine Palmitoyl Transferase-1 CPT-1)

Note: Do not confuse malonate with malate (intermediate in  the TCA cycle)




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 79, 158

questions.stem: Anaplerotic (gap-filling) reactions are the reactions that replenish the depleted TCA cycle intermediates that were used up in the biosynthesis reactions. Which of the following is the major anaplerotic enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyruvate carboxylase

Oxaloacetate (OAA) is regarded as a carrier and 1st substrate of the TCA cycle. Thus, the production of oxaloacetate is the major anaplerotic reaction.

questions.stem: TCA reactions are happening in the mitochondrial matrix for effective utilization, of reduced coenzymes generated in TCA, by ETC. All of the following TCA cycle dehydrogenases are located in the mitochondrial matrix, EXCEPT
questions.solutionHtml:
Succinate dehydrogenase
  • Aka succinate-coenzyme Q reductase or respiratory complex II is embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
  • It is the only enzyme that simultaneously takes part in TCA, ETC
  • The FAD cofactor is covalently attached to this enzyme.
  • The electrons transferred from the succinate are directly feed in to ETC through the reduced coenzyme FADH2.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 159

questions.stem: In the TCA cycle, two molecules of CO2 are produced along with the generation of reducing equivalents NADH and FADH2. Simultaneous oxidation and decarboxylation happen in the reaction catalyzed by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase
  • Simultaneous removal of electrons and CO2 from a substrate is called Oxidative
  • There are total 4 dehydrogenases present in Kreb's cycle:
    • Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)
    • α- Ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (α-KG DH)
    • Succinate dehydrogenase
    • Malate dehydrogenase
  • Out of them, two catalyzes oxidative decarboxylation reactions:
    • Isocitrate dehydrogenase
    • α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 158

questions.stem: All of the following are tightly bound to component enzymes of pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, EXCEPT:
questions.solutionHtml:
Coenzyme A
  • CoA is a loosely bound cofactor of PDH component E2
  • Help enzyme in catalysis by accepting acetyl group from lipoamide
  • Another loosely bound cofactor is NAD which is a cofactor of the E3 subunit of the enzyme

questions.stem: An individual display lactic acidemia as well as reduced activity of α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase. The most likely single enzymatic mutation that leads to these changes would be in which one of the following proteins?

options.label: A
options.text: The E3 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase

options.label: B
options.text: The E1 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase

options.label: C
options.text: The E2 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase

questions.answerText: The E3 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase
questions.solutionHtml:
The E3 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase
  • The E3 subunit of pyruvate dehydrogenase, the dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase activity (with bound FAD), is identical to α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.
  • Mutation in this subunit would lead to an accumulation of pyruvate (because pyruvate dehydrogenase activity is reduced), and the accumulated pyruvate is converted to lactate.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 163, 168

questions.stem: The TCA cycle is a common link between various metabolic pathways and plays a vital role in cell metabolism. The unavailability of which of the following will most adversely affect the TCA cycle:
questions.solutionHtml:
Oxaloacetate

Regulation of the TCA cycle:

TCA is a vital cycle with no hormonal control. However, some control is exerted by:

  • Energy Status of the cell
  • Availability of Oxaloacetate (not acetyl CoA)
  • TCA is always active whether fed or fasting state
  • However, it can get slower or faster depending on the availability of oxaloacetate.
  • So, Oxaloacetate is regarded as:
    • Carrier of TCA cycle
    • 1st substrate of TCA
    • catalytic role in TCA



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 162

questions.stem: In the citric acid cycle, fumarate is converted to malate by the enzyme fumarase. This enzyme is an example of which of the following category of enzymes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lyase

questions.stem: Which one of the following conditions decreases the oxidation of acetyl CoA by the citric acid cycle?

options.label: B
options.text: A low NADH due to rapid oxidization to NAD+ through the respiratory chain

questions.solutionHtml:
A low NAD+/NADH ratio
  • Covalent modification by the two regulatory enzymes that are part of the complex alternately activate and inactivate E1 (PDH).
  • The cyclic AMP-independent PDH kinase phosphorylates and, thereby, inhibits E1, whereas PDH phosphatase dephosphorylates and activates E1.
  • The kinase itself is allosterically activated by ATP, acetyl CoA, and NADH. Therefore, in the presence of these high-energy signals, the PDH complex is turned off.
  • Pyruvate is a potent inhibitor of PDH kinase. Therefore, if pyruvate concentrations are elevated, E1 will be maximally active.
  • Calcium is a strong activator of PDH phosphatase, stimulating E1 activity.
  • This is particularly important in skeletal muscle, where the release of Ca2+ during contraction stimulates the PDH complex, thereby energy production.
  • Although covalent regulation by the kinase and phosphatase is key, the complex is also subject to product (NADH, acetyl CoA) inhibition.




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 111

questions.stem: Each round of TCA involves two oxidative decarboxylation reactions. 2 carbon atoms that are lost as CO2 are derived from:
questions.solutionHtml:
Oxaloacetate
  • In the first round of the TCA cycle, the 2 Cs of acetyl CoA are transferred to oxaloacetate and are not released as CO2.
  • In the 2nd round of the cycle, Cs from OAA and acetyl CoA are mixed and CO2 released may have C from Oxaloacetate or acetyl CoA.
  • So, the best answer is oxaloacetate >>Acetyl CoA



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 158

questions.stem: As a general rule, rate-limiting steps or enzymes are generally considered the regulatory steps of any metabolic pathway. which of the following is the RLE of TCA?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • TCA is a vital pathway and is always active whether fed or fasting state
  • So, it is not controlled by hormones
  • However, the enzymes activity is affected by the availability of substrate
  • 3 enzymes that are rate-limiting in the TCA cycle

Citrate Synthase

  • First enzyme and catalyzes the condensation of acetyl CoA and oxaloacetate
  • Inhibitors: NADH, succinyl-CoA, citrate, ATP
  • Activators: ADP

Isocitrate Dehydrogenase

  • catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate to α-Ketoglutarate
  • Inhibitors: ATP
  • Activators: ADP, Ca2+

Alpha-Ketoglutarate Dehydrogenase

  • catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of α-Ketoglutarate to succinyl CoA
  • Inhibitors: NADH, succinyl-CoA
  • Activators: Ca2+



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 162

questions.stem: A male child of age 2.6 years was taken to the hospital with manifestations of poor diet intake, nausea, abdominal pain, poor growth, occasional loss of consciousness, and rapid breathing. Clinical examination and tests revealed the presence of lactic acidosis, Hyperammonemia, prominent forehead, flared nostrils, and hypotonia. Plasma lactate, plasma pyruvate, plasma ammonia, and MRI were performed. The child was diagnosed with congenital deficiency of an enzyme mainly responsible for link reaction between metabolite of glycolysis and substrate of the TCA cycle. The diet which will be least helpful in the treatment of this patient will be:
questions.solutionHtml:
Carbohydrate-rich diet
  • Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency (also known as pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency or PDCD) is a rare neurodegenerative disorder associated with abnormal mitochondrial metabolism.
  • The PDC is a multi-enzyme complex that plays a vital role as a key regulatory step in the central pathways of energy metabolism in the mitochondria. The disorder shows heterogeneous characteristics in both clinical presentation and biochemical abnormality.
  • In PDH def, a carbohydrate-rich diet will result in the formation of a high concentration of pyruvate which will get converted into lactate and exaggerate the symptoms of lactic acidosis.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 168, 169

questions.stem: One of the major roles of the TCA cycle is to generate reduced cofactors for ATP production from oxidative phosphorylation. The net ATP yield when one molecule of pyruvate is completely oxidized to CO2 & H2O is:
questions.solutionHtml:
12.5

The question says complete oxidation of pyruvate and not glucose, so we have to start with pyruvate without considering the glycolysis part.

Net ATPs produced = 2.5 + 7.5 + 1.5 + 1.0 =12.5 ATPs





Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 164

questions.stem: Child of age 5 months was taken to the hospital with lethargy, vomiting and abnormally rapid breathing, and poor feeding. The infant exhibited signs of hypotonia, tachypnea, poor cognitive functions, mental retardation, and motor abnormalities. Examination and tests concluded the diagnosis of congenital lactic acidosis. Select the correct statement?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency
  • Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDC) deficiency is a genetic mitochondrial disease of carbohydrate metabolism that is due to a mutation in mtDNA. It is generally considered to be the most common cause of biochemically proven cases of congenital lactic acidosis. PDC deficiency can be inherited as an autosomal recessive or X-linked recessive trait.
  • Most cases of congenital lactic acidosis are caused by one or more inherited mutations of genes within the DNA located within the nucleus (nDNA) or within the mitochondria (mtDNA) of cells.
  • Genes carry the genetic instructions for cells. A mutation is a change in a gene located in nuclear or mitochondrial DNA that may cause disease
  • Mutations affecting the genes for mitochondria (mtDNA) are inherited from the mother. mtDNA that is found in sperm cells is typically lost during fertilization.
  • As a result, all human mtDNA comes from the mother. An affected mother will pass on the mutation to all her children, but only her daughters will pass on the mutation to their children.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 168-169
